title: RiskEngine Methodology Notes
body:
Author: Owen Gallagher, Head of Risk
Last updated: 2026-07-03
Owner team: Risk
Audience: Risk, Trading, Wealth Management, Operations, Compliance, Technology

Purpose
These notes describe how RiskEngine produces intraday Value at Risk (VaR) and exposure figures, which inputs it relies on, and where the numbers surface in ReportingBI. They are meant to help desk heads, analysts and engineers interpret the outputs correctly and know who to contact when something looks off. No client-level data is reproduced here; where a client needs to be discussed, use the client reference id in ClientHub.

Scope and Upstream Dependencies
RiskEngine is a critical system owned by Risk. It consumes two upstream feeds: prices and valuations from PricingSvc, and holdings from PositionStore. PricingSvc in turn depends on MarketDataFeed, so a stale exchange or vendor feed will eventually show up as stale risk. If either PricingSvc or PositionStore is degraded, RiskEngine flags the affected run as partial rather than silently using old data.

VaR Approach
The primary measure is one-day historical simulation VaR at 99% confidence, using a rolling window of 500 business days of risk-factor returns. Returns are absolute for rates and spreads, and relative for equities, FX and commodities. Scenarios are equally weighted. We do not apply decay weighting in the headline number, though a 94% exponentially weighted variant is calculated alongside it as a sensitivity and is available to Paul Hansen and the market risk team on request.

We also report 95% VaR and expected shortfall at 97.5%. Expected shortfall is the figure we look at first when the desk has concentrated or option-heavy books, because VaR alone understates tail behavior there.

Run Cadence
Full revaluation runs happen at the start of day, using the prior close snapshot from PositionStore. Intraday refreshes run every 15 minutes between market open and close. Intraday runs use delta-gamma approximations for option positions and full revaluation only for the top positions by notional. The end-of-day run uses full revaluation for everything and is the version that feeds regulatory and management reporting.

Exposure Measures
Beyond VaR, RiskEngine publishes gross and net exposure by desk, by asset class and by issuer. Single-issuer concentration is measured against the limit framework approved by the risk committee. Counterparty exposure is calculated as current mark-to-market plus a simple add-on by product type; Credit Risk (Lance Peters, Phillip Jackson, John Garcia) owns the add-on table and reviews it quarterly.

Limits and Escalation
Desk VaR limits are set by Risk with input from Daniel Reyes for Trading. A breach is defined as the intraday 99% VaR exceeding the limit on two consecutive refreshes. A single-refresh excursion is logged but not escalated unless it exceeds 120% of limit. Escalation path:
1. Market Risk (Paul Hansen) contacts the desk head.
2. If unresolved within 30 minutes, Owen Gallagher is informed.
3. Persistent breaches are reported to Martin Osei and noted in the daily risk summary.

Backtesting
We compare daily P&L against the prior day's 99% VaR. Exceptions are counted over a trailing 250 business days. Four or fewer exceptions is green, five to nine is amber, ten or more is red. Each exception is documented with cause: market move, position change after the snapshot, or model or data issue. Amber and red results are reviewed with Compliance before being included in regulatory reporting.

Known Limitations
Intraday delta-gamma approximation can understate risk in large moves for barrier and short-dated options. Illiquid instruments use proxy series, which dampens measured volatility. Positions booked after the snapshot are not reflected until the next intraday refresh. Wealth Management portfolios in PortfolioMgr are covered at an aggregated level and are not part of desk VaR.

Reporting in ReportingBI
ReportingBI reads RiskEngine output together with GLCore and DataLake. The risk dashboards display the end-of-day figures, not the latest intraday refresh, unless the tile is labeled intraday. If a dashboard number differs from the RiskEngine console, check the run timestamp first, then whether the run was marked partial.

Change Control
Any change to the window length, confidence level, scenario weighting or proxy mapping requires model validation sign-off from Risk and notice to Trading and Operations at least five business days before release. Engineering changes to the service itself go through the standard release process with Technology, and Sam Okafor's team is the contact for deployment questions.

Contacts
